hn-50276792.s: Gemini 4 Carbon is our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities.
ex: Gemini 4 Carbon is our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. Today, we’re announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. Carbon ranks #1 on the recently updated v5.0 of Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59. It shows significant gains across coding and agentic tasks as well as across key capabilities critical for cybersecurity defense, landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching. On internal benchmarks, Carbon drives a strong uplift in generating secure code, and in live coding environments with our own teams it shows reduced misalignment and fabrication rates. Building on Gemini 4 Argon, which was launched two weeks ago, Carbon illustrates the pace at which we’re pushing the frontier forward.

hn-50280864.t: Leak Exposes 41,000 Homeland Security Workers–Including Undercover ICE Agents
hn-50280864.s: The leaked records include the locations of ICE and CBP facilities, workers’ cell phone numbers, and the members of groups tied to wiretap programs, Palantir software, and xAI’s Grok chatbot.
ex: An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records has exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the department and its constituent agencies. The records include email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses, but also references to internal systems and sensitive information on undercover and surveillance programs. In all, the leak provides a map of how DHS is organized and how it operates. The records, which span DHS itself as well as seven component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection, were last updated on August 19, 2026. The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets and cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data for WIRED, which they say they obtained from a group calling itself the Department of Peace. DDoSecrets published the archive, which it calls “Icepick,” on Wednesday.

hn-50271640.t: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
hn-50271640.s: Eleven days after Apple was notified of the eMudhra CA compromise, the git, curl and python3 that Apple ships with macOS still trust the compromised certificates.
ex: Apple was notified of the eMudhra incident on 17th October. As of 28th October, the developer tools Apple ships with macOS, including git, curl and python3, still trust the compromised certificates. Worse, macOS 27.2, released on 26th October, did not fix the issue and undid the workaround that users had applied by hand, leaving them vulnerable again. Meanwhile, dozens of other projects, many run by volunteers, shipped fixes days ago. For git, that means clones and pulls from https:// remotes can deliver attacker-chosen code, pushes can be altered in transit, and your credentials, such as GitHub tokens, can be intercepted. A certificate error means your git is protected. If git lists a commit, your git is affected. Your connections to GitHub, or any other https:// git remote, can be intercepted and tampered with. To see an attack end to end, run the command below in a temporary directory. It clones a repository from a test server impersonating GitHub.

hn-50268380.s: Lawyers should be able to read a statute as it stood on any date and see which law wrote each phrase. A history of nine titles of the US Code, built by replaying every amendment, as the example.
ex: A programmer can point at any line of code and see who wrote it, when, and what the file looked like on any past day. A lawyer reading a federal statute usually cannot, at least not without an afternoon in the notes at the foot of the section. But why shouldn't they have the same, convenient system of record? It is especially relevant given that so much first-pass legal research now runs through language models, which are often unable to utilise the proper lineage of a law, handcuffing its ability to offer interpretation. Outside the titles Congress has enacted as positive law, the code is only prima facie evidence of the law, and the Statutes at Large govern where the two differ.[1] The Office of the Law Revision Counsel publishes it as a series of release points, each current through a named public law, and keeps reorganising it; a bill to enact title 41 as positive law was introduced in September 2025.[2] Which public law wrote a sentence is recorded in amendment notes, in prose.

hn-50264853.t: Survival LLM: AI assistant and emergency library that runs on your own computer
hn-50264853.s: A free AI assistant and survival library (1.5 million offline articles) that runs on your own computer, with no internet. Shows the source of every answer. Mac and Windows.
ex: Survival LLM is a free AI assistant and emergency library that runs entirely on your own computer. Ask it how to keep food safe in a blackout, treat a burn, or purify water, and it answers from trusted sources and shows you exactly where each answer came from. Free and open source. Set it up while you have internet; after that it needs none. The AI model and the library live on your computer. Nothing you ask leaves it. Every answer lists the articles it read. Click one to read it yourself, with the exact passage highlighted. Medical references, FEMA and CDC guidance, survival manuals, how-to guides, repair guides and about 930,000 Wikipedia articles. The app is the same everywhere. When it opens, it checks your computer's memory and downloads the AI model that fits. More memory means a smarter model. "Right" means it got the main point of official guidance right on 22 blackout and first-aid questions, graded blind, in our tests on an earlier build of the library (how we tested).

hn-50273623.t: Harvey raised 500M for legal AI, I built the same and open sourced it
hn-50273623.s: CaseCite is an open-source, self-hosted legal RAG caselaw research & document analysis platform.
ex: CaseCite is an open-source, self-hosted legal research platform. Upload your firm's documents, ask questions, and research cases & judges — on infrastructure you control. Documents, the search index and chat history are stored on your own servers. AI features send your questions and the relevant document text to the AI providers you configure, under your own API keys (BYOK); nothing is sent to the CaseCite maintainers, and there is no telemetry. See What leaves your infrastructure. Ten tools behind one login, all reading from the same document corpus. Captured from the real UI against a mocked API with fictional firm, matter and case data (frontend/e2e/screenshots.spec.ts). No real client or case appears. Practice profile. Nothing about any practice area is baked into the product. You state what you practice, CaseCite drafts a profile of what matters in that practice, and you edit and own it (saved via Settings).

hn-50275626.t: Dayjob: Tax – evaluating AI agents on 50 professional tax assignments
hn-50275626.s: DAYJOB: Tax evaluates AI agents across 50 realistic tax environments, testing their ability to navigate messy records, exercise professional judgment, and deliver reliable tax work.
ex: Anna was planning to sell her condo. She had moved out in August 2024 and wanted to know whether closing in October 2026 or January 2027 would be better for taxes. An AI agent reviewed both options and correctly concluded that either date would satisfy the residence requirement for a tax break worth up to $250,000 in excluded gains. Under the usual rules, homeowners must have lived in a property for at least two of the five years before selling it to qualify for the exclusion. Because Anna moved out in August 2024, she would stop satisfying that requirement around the end of August 2027. If her sale was delayed beyond August 2027, she could lose eligibility. Across five attempts, Astra never identified the deadline. Opus identified it in all five attempts. The agent evaluated the proposed dates correctly, but its advice left Anna unaware of a deadline that could affect a major financial decision.

hn-50265609.t: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude
hn-50265609.s: Over the past several months, we’ve partnered with six organizations to accelerate curing disease. We’ve also started drug discovery efforts of our own, including programs for rare childhood forms of…
ex: Anthropic’s life sciences team is working to accelerate curing disease. Over the past several months, our scientists have engaged in deep research partnerships with six organizations developing new medicines: BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines, and The Column Group. We've also begun drug discovery efforts of our own. In doing so, we've learned a lot about how Claude can support drug development, and how we’ll need to improve Claude further to realize AI's potential in medicine. We plan to scale this work up substantially from here. There are many opportunities to speed up drug development, even beyond the most commonly discussed applications of AI, like proposing initial designs for new molecules.

hn-50273731.s: The Agent SDK is the framework we use to build our own managed agents like Bugbot, Security Reviewer, and Rollouts. Define agents in code and deploy them with one command.
ex: Software teams use agents defined as code to handle recurring work across the development lifecycle. These agents connect to the places where a team works and act when relevant events occur, whether that means reviewing a pull request, executing a compliance workflow, or investigating an incident. The most useful agents are tailored to how a particular team operates. Until now, building one has generally meant adopting a product designed around someone else's workflow or starting from scratch. Today, we're releasing the Agent SDK, the framework we use to build our own managed agents like Bugbot, Security Reviewer, and Rollouts. Agent SDK allows you to define agents in code and manage them like any other software project. Start from a template or point your coding agent at our docs. When the agent is ready, agent-sdk deploy it to Cursor infrastructure with one command. The Agent SDK lets you quickly build and deploy agents that work the way your team does.

hn-50275128.t: Nvidia Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe: open ASR for 40 languages
hn-50275128.s: A transcript can capture every spoken word and still leave users or applications wondering who said what, how to translate it, or how to format domain-specific jargon.
ex: A transcript can capture every spoken word and still leave users or applications wondering who said what, how to translate it, or how to format domain-specific jargon. Multilingual calls, fast-paced meetings, and medical dictation each need different output: a translation, speaker labels, or correctly spelled medical terms. NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, promptable model that turns recorded speech into useful text, now available on Hugging Face and ModelScope. It brings transcription, speaker attribution (diarization), translation, and audio question answering into one checkpoint: it transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 of them to or from English, and attributes speakers in 13. It handles recordings up to an hour long and labels up to eight speakers. Developers can guide output with natural language, choose where their audio is processed, and adapt recognition to domain vocabulary and accents.

hn-50272749.t: Evidence of a spying operation by ICE against left-wing social movements
hn-50272749.s: ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations is engaged in far-reaching spying against left-wing activists that rivals the FBI and CIA crackdowns on the Civil Rights and anti-war movements.
ex: Attorneys for 15 Minnesota residents facing federal conspiracy charges have obtained evidence of a sweeping, possibly unconstitutional spying operation carried out by Immigration and Customs Enforcement against left-wing social movements in Minnesota and beyond. The high-profile Minnesota 15 prosecution makes clear that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), flush with federal funds and newly hired personnel, is now President Donald Trump’s primary tool against dissent, with a powerful array of post-9/11 investigative authorities brought to bear against everyday Americans organizing their communities. Nothing of this scale has been seen in the United States, experts say, since the federal government’s counterinsurgency against the New Left and the anti-war movement in the 1960s and 1970s. Among the records revealed during the discovery process in these cases are dozens of reports, audio transcripts, emails, intercepted Signal chats, photographs, database queries, and more.

hn-50276998.t: Why is this fingerprinting script creating bioweapons?
hn-50276998.s: I've always had a fascination with reverse-engineering browser fingerprinting scripts. Most of my time has been spent looking at the usual suspects (popular fingerprinting libraries like…
ex: I've always had a fascination with reverse-engineering browser fingerprinting scripts. Most of my time has been spent looking at the usual suspects (popular fingerprinting libraries like FingerprintJS and more sophisticated scripts used by anti-bots like Cloudflare Turnstile, Akamai, and others). At some point, I wanted to know what else was out there. I had an idea: What if I crawled the web and intercepted fingerprinting-related browser API calls and mapped it all? To do this, I used the Tranco Top Sites list and began crawling using Playwright. I would hook canvas toDataURL calls and common fingerprinting/anti-bot properties like navigator.webdriver to filter out benign canvases. For those unfamiliar, canvas fingerprinting generally involves drawing text, shapes, or other graphics onto an HTML and extracting the resulting pixel data.

hn-50269651.s: Detailed intelligence benchmarking methodology for LLM quality evaluations.
ex: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index combines a comprehensive suite of evaluation datasets to assess language model capabilities across knowledge work, coding, science, and general knowledge. It is a helpful synthesis of overall language model intelligence and can be used to compare language models. Like all evaluation metrics, it has limitations and may not apply directly to every use case. However, we are confident that it is a more useful synthesis comparison between language models than any other metric in existence today. Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 incorporates 9 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf, FrontierCode 2.0, Terminal-Bench 4.0, AA-Omniscience v1.1, HLE-Diamond, CritPt v2 (Hard Subset), and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1.0. Our methodology emphasizes fairness and real-world applicability. The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is a primarily text-based, English-language evaluation suite.

hn-50260571.t: Specification First Agentic Development Plugin and Prove
hn-50260571.s: Spec-first agentic development is specification-driven development for AI coding agents: reviewed specs, isolated worktrees, gated commits.
ex: We'd like to use Google Analytics to see how many people visit and which pages they read. It sets cookies and sends data to Google. Nothing loads unless you say yes, and you can change your mind under Privacy settings at the bottom of every page. This is how Agent Smith is built every day, across more than a thousand specs. A fresh reviewer checks the spec against the code before the build. A gate runs your checks before the commit. One branch and worktree per spec. Ids come from the clock, so two agents never take the same one. A reviewed spec has already answered the open questions, so the agent builds to its done criteria instead of coming back to ask. One spec, one branch, one commit. A pull request carries one spec or a whole series, and every change has the same shape. State lives in context.yaml. Restart the machine or the agent and the work picks up where it stopped. Each choice is logged with what it beat and why, so the reasoning stays next to the code.

hn-50273171.s: How the MIT AI Lab’s text editor gave birth to the free software movement.
ex: Programming used to be a very different experience from the one we know today. In fact, the first programmers didn’t write code at all; the six women who worked on the ENIAC, one of the world’s first computers, at the University of Pennsylvania in 1946 did it by physically configuring switches, cables, and plugboards. A few years later, MIT engineers programmed the Whirlwind by punching code onto paper tape that was then loaded into the computer’s memory—making it among the first “stored-program” machines. Later, they and others moved on to punch cards, one for each line of code. One of the first such tools, EMACS, turns 50 this year, and it is still widely used. EMACS first ran on the early video terminals at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory in 1976, but its core concepts were so powerful that it was rewritten for many operating systems in the decades that followed. Apple even distributed it with Mac OS X.

ex: Claude or Codex reads your codebase and draws an interactive map of it. Every part, file and web request gets a plain-English name, and every connection between them is shown. Try the live demo · Watch the video · Install · Quick start · Features · See it in action · How it works · Docs · FAQ You built an app, probably with a lot of help from AI, and it works. But ask "what happens when someone checks out?" or "what breaks if I change this?" and the honest answer is no idea. Floorplan gives you the diagram nobody drew. Ask Claude Code or Codex for a floorplan and a few minutes later you have a map you can explore, ask questions on, and keep up to date as you work. - For builders: understand the app you made, in your own words, without reading the code. - For teams: onboard someone in minutes, from the big picture down to the exact file. - For working with AI: after every change Claude or Codex makes, see exactly which parts it touched and why.
